note: Riders, horses, horse casualties, dismounted fights and draught-horse losses of the batteries. Generated by tools/build-cavalry-horses.mjs from src/history/cavalry.mjs and the real history layer; nothing here is hand-edited. Every number carries its tier; the gaps are in gaps[] and in GOVERNANCE/horde/ws10-cavalry/proposed-register.

horse_observations.what: 10th New York Cavalry: 303 serviceable and 191 unserviceable horses for 460 men
horse_observations.note: magazine source; kit tier documented, support not verified here, so carried as inferred

horse_observations.what: an 8th New York company: 56 men with 43 horses
6th US Cavalry: about 500 serviceable horses of about 1,072 men assigned on June 5
horse_observations.note: blog source (weak): lead only, carried as an observation inside a range, never as a count

mounted_share.basis: range of the share of men with a serviceable horse: the lowest of three observed shares (CH-10NY 0.66, CH-8NY-CO 0.77, CH-6US 0.47) up to one horse for every man. The figure drawn is the upper end: one horse per drawn trooper.

observation.cite: OR Ser.I vol.27 pt.1, OR27-1-R343 Lieut. Nicholas Nolan, p. 948 (ledger claim POS-A-CV1-033, note)
observation.note: killed, wounded and missing, printed "290" with OCR digits; the only regimental horse figure in the position ledgers

perMan.basis: horses down per man down: bounds 0 (a man hit, the horse not: logical bound) and 292/290 (the single observation); the picture takes one horse down with each fallen trooper (the observation capped at 1)

holder.source: PDF B.2 July 1 (every fourth man holds horses); kit/cavalry_units.json behaviour_states horse_holding
holder.basis: one man in four holds the horses of the four (his own and the three comrades who fight); no cavalry manual page acquired

led_horses.basis: a model parameter with no source: the led horses stand 12 m behind the line (the carbine fire line is not documented to a distance) and are led there at a walk of about 1.7 m/s (the Wheeler walk, gaits.mjs), 7 s

dismounts.when_basis: the afternoon of July 1 (printed "in the afternoon"; the hours are the convention of the engagement clause)
dismounts.cite: OR27-1-R338 Col. William Gamble, p. 934: "Half of the Eighth New York, Third Indiana, and Twelfth Illinois were dismounted"
OR27-1-R339 Col. Thomas C. Devin, p. 938: "a squadron of the Sixth New York to the front and left as skirmishers" (6 companies printed by the kit; two companies to the squadron is assumed)
OR27-1-R339 Devin p. 939: "dismounting the rest of his available force" (no fraction printed)

dismounts.when_basis: the afternoon of July 3 until nightfall (printed)
dismounts.cite: OR27-1-R344 Brig. Gen. David McM. Gregg, p. 956: "the Third Pennsylvania Cavalry deployed as dismounted skirmishers" (no fraction printed; the whole regiment is the reading of the sentence)
OR27-1-R361 Brig. Gen. Custer, p. 998: the Fifth Michigan "dismounted on the left of the brigade" (no fraction printed)

dismounts.when_basis: the engagement at Hunterstown, July 2 (the hour is not printed)
dismounts.cite: OR27-1-R361 Custer p. 1000: the Seventh Michigan "excepting one squadron, was advanced as dismounted skirmishers" (10 companies printed by the kit; two to the squadron assumed)
Michigan at Gettysburg (1889) p. 139-142: "two squadrons dismounted" (a regimental history; the company count of the regiment is not in the kit)

dismounts.when_basis: July 3 before the charge at 5 p.m.
dismounts.cite: OR27-1-R365 Lieut. Col. Preston p. 1013: Companies A, D, E and I dismounted as skirmishers (the regiment's company count is not in the kit; OCR uncertain)

dismounts.when_basis: July 3 until the rounds were spent
dismounts.cite: Stuart's report (ledger D PD-cav-jenkins-01, OCR uncertain): Jenkins' brigade "fought dismounted until the rounds were spent"

gaps.title: Mounted strength of every cavalry regiment (horses per man)
gaps.text: No regimental present-for-duty or mounted strength is in the record (Busey and Martin print-only; kit strengths_note). Three weak observations bound the share of men with a serviceable horse from 0.47 to 0.77; the range card shows that share up to one horse per man and the picture draws one horse per drawn trooper.

gaps.title: Horse casualties of cavalry
gaps.text: One regimental horse figure is printed in the ledgers (6th US, 292 horses with 290 men, OCR digits). Horses killed under unhurt riders, horses lost with missing men, wounded horses led off and horse losses of the other regiments are not in the record and are not drawn; the time of each loss is the time of the rider's fall.

gaps.title: Led horses and horse-holders: distance and handling
gaps.text: One man in four holds the horses is the plan's statement (no cavalry manual page acquired, G-ANIM-08); the 12 m back and the 7 s to lead them there are model parameters. The sources acquired give no distance.

gaps.title: Dismounted shares: squadron arithmetic and unstated fractions
gaps.text: Where the report names squadrons the share rests on two companies to the squadron (not printed in any acquired text) and the kit's company count; where it names companies without a total (1st Vermont), a number of squadrons without a company count (6th Michigan) or says only "the rest" (9th New York) no fraction exists and the unit is drawn mounted with this gap listed. The hours of a fight are the engagement windows of the timeline rows (seeded_unverified).

gaps.title: Spare, remount, pack and officers' horses of cavalry
gaps.text: No acquired source gives spare or led horses of a cavalry regiment beyond the horses of the dismounted men (the artillery case, ws6-EG-05, rests on one forum quote). Remounts (about 17,000 to the Cavalry Corps May-July 1863, HistoryNet) are an aggregate, not a unit figure. No spare horse is drawn.

gaps.title: The mounted charge: path and full-speed pace
gaps.text: The charge clauses of the layer (AC-12, the Jul 3 15:00 attack of the 3rd Division) carry no path, so a charging unit has no ground speed and stands. The manual's schedule (Wheeler paras 292, 410-411: walk 20, trot 60, gallop 80, charge 60 paces) is data in gaits.mjs; the speed of the last pace ("nearly full speed", para 189) has no printed number. A unit whose path runs faster than the Wheeler gallop plays the gallop clip.

gaps.title: Cavalry that the layer does not draw
gaps.text: Of the 55 cavalry regiments and battalions of the order of battle, the real layer draws 21:  the 5 regiments of the Reserve Brigade, the 5 of McIntosh, the 4 of J. I. Gregg's, 6 of Hampton's and the 35th Virginia Battalion; Gamble's and Devin's regiments, Custer's Michigan Brigade, Farnsworth's brigade and the rest of Stuart's command have no road of approach or place in the ledgers and are drawn with 0 figures. This is the history layer's open gap, not narrowed here.

gaps.title: Draught-horse losses of the batteries: times
gaps.text: Counts are printed for six batteries (kit losses: 15th NY 25 killed or wounded, 1st NY B 13 disabled, 1st RI B 24 killed and 6 disabled, 4th NY 11, 13th NY 12, 2nd US A 13); no time is printed. Each loss is placed by the counter-based RNG inside the battery's engagement windows. 2nd US A (Calef, horse artillery) is not a drawn leaf unit of the layer.
